title: skill-compiler: compile skills into validated cached adapters, with pool-attested pass verification
body: Port of fork PR 12 (the contributor's fork) onto current upstream/main. Rebuilt in a worktree by cherry-picking only the branch's own commits, so it carries none of the fork main's history. Own test suites run locally and pass on the branch. Companion upstream PRs replace the fifteen fork PRs that were opened in the wrong place.
source: On 2026-10-22 the maintainer delegated judging and fixes to the review loop. Codex and the original gpt-6-astra session checked every final finding and excluded proposal against the exact reviewed head, carrying forward earlier decisions and using bounded synthetic reproductions. Judgments are delegated agent decisions, not individually maintainer-confirmed labels. One must/medium was reproduced: concurrent same-basename harvests mix history. The case base is the PR merge-base; integration target is eab04ad4097fb2030f27bee6026e24f57289f12d. GitHub body edit history was empty; identifying names are generalized as in the previous case. All 224 original proposals, including 114 outside the final list, were assessed. 55 final findings repeat or overlap prior decisions. The collected prior context contained 30 kept decisions and omitted 98 under its cap; this limits what the automatic review could suppress. Evaluation: https://github.com/laude-institute/headlong/pull/156#issuecomment-6340048010. Fix: 3ded6457ace075c0ae64f07bbbbf5ef80fa215e5. Optional suggestions remain deferred. No merge or approval.

findings.label: invalid
findings.what: resolve_skill unpacks its argv wrongly, so the refuse list and the root list are shifted. The heredoc is invoked as `python3 - "$1" "$SKILLS_DIR" "$KERNEL_DIR" "$COMPILE_SKIP_SKILLS"`, and the script does `name, *roots, refused = sys.argv[1:]`. That assigns `name`=$1, `roots`=[SKILLS_DIR], and `refused`=KERNEL_DIR: the refused set is the kernel directory path and KERNEL_DIR is never searched for skills. So the frontmatter/name guard compares a skill name against a path (never matches) and skills that live only in the kernel tree report "Skill not found". The script should take `name, refused, *roots` or reorder the arguments.

findings.what: Operator config is sourced as shell code and its key values are exported even when not on the allow-list. In `_sc_operator_config`, each key found in `cwd/.env` or `${SHELLM_CONF_DIR:-state}/.env` is resolved by `val=$(set -a; . "$envfile" ...)` — the whole file is executed as shell for every key, and then `export "$key=$val"`. The key list comes from a loose sed over arbitrary names, so any variable the file assigns (e.g. `IDENTITY_DIR`, `TRAJ_DIR`, `LLM_USAGE_LEDGER`, or a function/command substitution expression) is evaluated and produced. `_sc_load_operator_config` re-exports the values into the runner environment before `_sc_isolate_state` runs. The comment claims only `config_keys` are emitted, but values are only filtered later by `for key in $config_keys`, so a `.env` can steer selectors and paths that the isolation step is supposed to neutralise. Impact is limited to a `.env` the operator already controls, but the guard and the documented contract disagree with the behaviour.

findings.what: Quote-fold test asserts a pass on a command that only appears in the docs, not a pinned command line. The test's stated purpose is that a pinned command line passes when the agent writes the other quote style. But the compile in STUB_MODE=quote uses fixture-greet, whose SKILL.md contains no `sed` command at all, and whose script prints only the greeting; the stub's trajectory output is `stripped with sed 's/<[^>]*>//g'`. So the expect_contains literal is neither a pinned command nor in the phrase pool, and `.tests[0].pass == true` can only hold through the general INVENTED-with-final-output pass path, not through quote-fold matching. The check cannot fail if quote folding is broken.

findings.label: valid
findings.what: The direct Python regression harness fails obscurely when jq is absent instead of reporting the missing prerequisite.

found_by.text: REAL_JQ may be None and is exported into the harness env, breaking every jq stub call. shutil.which('jq') returns None when jq is not on PATH, and Case.__init__ then puts REAL_JQ=None into self.env for every subprocess. subprocess.run raises TypeError when an env value is not str/bytes/os.PathLike, so on any machine without jq every regression case fails with a Python traceback instead of a clear 'jq missing' diagnostic; there is no guard before STUBS.mkdir or the Case runs.

Scratch stubs dir cannot be reused and missing jq fails obscurely. The module creates its stub directory with STUBS.mkdir() (line 17) instead of mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True): re-running the suite against an existing scratch root fails before any check runs. This matters because the docstring states the checks can be re-pointed at a copy of the pre-fix compiler, which means running the same ROOT twice. Additionally, Case.__init__ reads REAL_JQ = shutil.which('jq') without a check; when jq is absent the jq stub's os.execv(os.environ['REAL_JQ']) raises TypeError instead of producing a clear skip, while test_skill_compiler.sh's header lists jq as a dependency.

Case root directories are created with mkdir() and fail on a re-run against the same ROOT. ROOT is created with exist_ok=True but each Case does self.root.mkdir() and STUBS.mkdir() without exist_ok, and direct_cache creates copy.mkdir(); if the harness is pointed at an existing scratch directory (the docstring says the checks can be pointed at a copy of the pre-fix compiler) the first Case raises FileExistsError, which check() swallows into a FAIL for every case.
